scope: positive-rational LN/LOG symbolic carriers and finite-scale materialization on governed Enterprise Math research paths
purpose: Extend the exact-arithmetic BRC materialization boundary to natural and arbitrary-base logarithms without native float/Decimal/Fraction state or exponential-size precision powers.
authority_note: This is an operational computation policy. It does not modify the canonical R023 Boolean-support theorem family, prove a logarithm-collapse theorem, add multiplicity/weight semantics to Boolean support, or grant Foundation status.

native_states.log: LOG_base(DIV(numerator, denominator)) with base carried as a positive rational DIV state
requirements: argument numerator is positive and denominator is positive
base numerator and denominator are positive
construction does not evaluate logarithm digits

ln_evaluation.orientation: For x below one, evaluate the positive magnitude ln(1/x) and retain a separate negative sign. For x above one, retain positive sign. x=1 is exact zero.
ln_evaluation.range_reduction: Choose integer k with 2^k <= y < 2^(k+1) for y=max(x,1/x), then write y=2^k*r with 1<=r<2.
ln_evaluation.combination: Bounds for abs(ln x) are k times the corresponding ln(2) bounds plus the reduced-ratio bounds.
ln_evaluation.native_representation: Every partial sum and remainder majorant is carried as an unreduced non-negative integer numerator/positive denominator pair. No quotient is materialized merely to form the bound.

finite_scale_collapse.scale: Any positive arbitrary-precision integer; decimal readout uses scale=10^digits.
finite_scale_collapse.cell_rule: Refine exact rational lower/upper bounds until BRC division of scale*lower and scale*upper yields one common magnitude cell index q, certifying q <= scale*abs(value) < q+1.
finite_scale_collapse.signed_readout: The native trace stores sign plus non-negative magnitude cell. Human decimal text uses truncation toward zero; the exact rational interval remains the evidence.
minimum_trace: exact rational lower and upper bounds
BRC division traces for lower and upper cell selection
exact-boundary marker and optional power-relation proof

arbitrary_base_log.identity: abs(log_b x)=abs(ln x)/abs(ln b); sign is sign(ln x)*sign(ln b).
arbitrary_base_log.interval_rule: For positive magnitude intervals Lx<=abs(ln x)<=Ux and Lb<=abs(ln b)<=Ub with Lb>0, use Lx/Ub <= abs(log_b x) <= Ux/Lb as exact rational carriers.
arbitrary_base_log.exact_grid_boundary_problem: An exact rational logarithm such as log_4(2)=1/2 can remain on a finite-scale cell boundary forever if only two-sided analytic intervals are refined.
arbitrary_base_log.boundary_resolution: When adjacent cells straddle candidate q/scale, reduce q/scale=m/n. Instead of constructing x^n or b^m, reduce the positive rational carriers and certify x=c^m and b=c^n for one common rational c using existing BRC perfect-power/root traces. This proves x^n=b^m and therefore exact boundary equality.
arbitrary_base_log.reuse: Boundary resolution composes existing DIV reduction and ROOT perfect-power BRC facades; it does not create a new root primitive.

complexity_boundary.forbidden_naive_precision_scheme: Do not certify d decimal digits by directly constructing x^(10^d) and b^q; the exponent-scale integer size is exponentially inappropriate for precision refinement.
complexity_boundary.current_scheme: After binary range reduction, z<=1/3 so the atanh remainder contracts geometrically. Term count is adaptively doubled until one BRC precision cell or an exact power-relation boundary is proved.
complexity_boundary.no_project_digit_ceiling: No mathematical digit ceiling is imposed. Resource exhaustion remains an implementation condition and may not be silently converted into false precision.

hard_boundaries: No real logarithm is defined here for zero or negative arguments.
Complex logarithm branches are outside V1 and must be separately typed.
The canonical R023 Boolean-support BRC carrier still does not preserve multiplicity, provenance, probability/weights, or signed/amplitude cancellation.
A future log-weight or log-semiring branch semantics would require a separately declared weighted carrier and theorem surface; it is not implied by this runtime facade.

tool_reuse_resolution.how_applied_or_why_not: T5 supplies finite integer precision/refinement, BRC division chooses certified precision cells, existing ROOT BRC resolves exact rational log boundaries, and all analytic bounds remain exact integer ratios. No new general-purpose arithmetic oracle is introduced.
tool_reuse_resolution.hard_boundary_checked: Operational logarithm materialization does not upgrade Boolean-support BRC to weighted or multiplicity-aware semantics and does not assert a logarithm-collapse theorem.
